### FIRE

Checking the relationship between FIRE battery and respondents across race. Why? I'm trying to decide whether these are appropriate controls to include in my policy analyses and deservingness score analyses. The batery was constructed to capture contemporary white racial attitudes. 

If I include them, I should be able to explain what it means to apply these (or some combination, maybe just one) of these controls to white respondents and non-white respondents. 

But equally as important is that I need to clarify why these are appropriate controls given my question and theory. 

My supposition is that experience with the carceral state might:
- shape policy preferences because 

(a) it distributes information. I expect this information -> more support for policies that distribute rights and resources
-> more certainty in support for less visible and "harder" issues. 

(b1) information may acculuate/ be interpreted into distinct frameworks for understanding ie scripts

(b2) information may acculuate/ be interpreted into institutional distrust  --> question dominant messages and scripts (would expect to deserving social construction scores that are fairly significantly higher for targets)

but there's also this element of race-class subjugation. Soss and Weaver might push back on this (RCS is relational, not like a single positivist measure), but if communities of color already have more proximal and direct exposure, they might already have different knowledge frameworks for interpretation (this also is Cohen & L). They would be more likely to understand race as important -- or their "script" would be one of more recognition of systemic racism or institutionalized racism -- in some ways, an opposing script fromt he standard punitive/personal responsibility script. 

# alternative

```{r}

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 1. Define variables and model waves
# ------------------------------------------------------------

# Focal demographic predictors
demo_controls <- c(
  "Black",
  "Hisp_Latino",
  "AllOthers"
)

demo_controls_labels <- c(
  Black = "Black",
  Hisp_Latino = "Hispanic/Latino",
  AllOthers = "Other RID"
)

# Party controls
party_controls <- c(
  "Republican",
  "Democrat"
)

# Party and ideology controls
party_ideo_controls <- c(
  "Republican",
  "Democrat",
  "fiscal_ideology",
  "social_ideology"
)

# FIRE dependent variables
fire_controls <- c(
  "fire_rare",
  "fire_privilege",
  "fire_angry",
  "fire_fear"
)

fire_controls_labels <- c(
  fire_rare = "Racism rare",
  fire_privilege = "White privilege",
  fire_angry = "Angry about racism",
  fire_fear = "Fear other races"
)

# Three specifications
fire_control_waves <- list(
  nocontrol = character(0),
  pid_wave = party_controls,
  pid_ideo_wave = party_ideo_controls
)

fire_wave_order <- c(
  "nocontrol",
  "pid_wave",
  "pid_ideo_wave"
)

fire_wave_labels <- c(
  nocontrol = "Demographics only",
  pid_wave = "Party ID",
  pid_ideo_wave = "Party and ideology"
)


# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 2. Function to estimate one model
# ------------------------------------------------------------

make_fire_model <- function(
    df,
    dv,
    ivs = demo_controls,
    controls = character(0)
) {

  # Include ALL demographic predictors in every model
  rhs <- c(ivs, controls)

  fml <- stats::reformulate(
    termlabels = rhs,
    response = dv
  )

  lm(fml, data = df)
}


# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 3. Estimate and store models by wave
# ------------------------------------------------------------

fire_dummies_waves <- list()

for (wave_name in fire_wave_order) {

  model_list <- list()

  # One regression per FIRE dependent variable
  for (dv in fire_controls) {

    model_name <- paste0("m_", dv)

    model_list[[model_name]] <- make_fire_model(
      df = sample_no_dk,
      dv = dv,
      ivs = demo_controls,
      controls = fire_control_waves[[wave_name]]
    )
  }

  fire_dummies_waves[[wave_name]] <- model_list
}


# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 4. Formatting helpers
# ------------------------------------------------------------

p_to_stars <- function(p) {
  dplyr::case_when(
    is.na(p) ~ "",
    p < .001 ~ "***",
    p < .01 ~ "**",
    p < .05 ~ "*",
    TRUE ~ ""
  )
}

fmt_num <- function(x, digits = 3) {
  ifelse(
    is.na(x),
    "",
    sprintf(paste0("%.", digits, "f"), x)
  )
}


# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 5. Extract one demographic coefficient from a model
# ------------------------------------------------------------

extract_fire_wave_stats <- function(
    dv_name,
    iv_name,
    wave_name,
    model_waves = fire_dummies_waves,
    robust = TRUE
) {

  # Each model now includes all three demographics
  model_name <- paste0("m_", dv_name)

  if (!wave_name %in% names(model_waves)) {
    stop("Wave not found: ", wave_name)
  }

  model_list <- model_waves[[wave_name]]

  if (!model_name %in% names(model_list)) {
    stop(
      "Model not found in wave '",
      wave_name, "': ", model_name
    )
  }

  mod <- model_list[[model_name]]

  # Extract coefficients with HC1 robust SEs by default
  if (robust) {

    ct <- lmtest::coeftest(
      mod,
      vcov. = sandwich::vcovHC(mod, type = "HC1")
    )

  } else {

    ct <- summary(mod)$coefficients

  }

  coef_table <- data.frame(
    term = rownames(ct),
    estimate = ct[, 1],
    std.error = ct[, 2],
    p.value = ct[, 4],
    row.names = NULL
  )

  # Find the requested demographic coefficient
  if (!iv_name %in% coef_table$term) {
    stop(
      "Term '", iv_name,
      "' not found in model ", model_name
    )
  }

  focal_row <- coef_table[
    coef_table$term == iv_name,
    ,
    drop = FALSE
  ]

  tibble::tibble(
    dv = dv_name,
    dv_label = fire_controls_labels[[dv_name]],
    iv = iv_name,
    iv_label = demo_controls_labels[[iv_name]],
    wave = wave_name,
    wave_label = fire_wave_labels[[wave_name]],
    estimate = focal_row$estimate,
    std.error = focal_row$std.error,
    p.value = focal_row$p.value,
    n = stats::nobs(mod),
    r2 = summary(mod)$r.squared
  )
}


# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 6. Gather demographic coefficients across all three waves
#    for one FIRE dependent variable
# ------------------------------------------------------------

make_wave_results_long <- function(
    dv_name,
    model_waves = fire_dummies_waves,
    row_vars = demo_controls,
    waves = fire_wave_order,
    robust = TRUE
) {

  if (!dv_name %in% fire_controls) {
    stop("DV not found in fire_controls: ", dv_name)
  }

  rows <- lapply(row_vars, function(iv_name) {

    wave_rows <- lapply(waves, function(wave_name) {

      extract_fire_wave_stats(
        dv_name = dv_name,
        iv_name = iv_name,
        wave_name = wave_name,
        model_waves = model_waves,
        robust = robust
      )
    })

    dplyr::bind_rows(wave_rows)
  })

  dplyr::bind_rows(rows) %>%
    dplyr::mutate(
      iv = factor(iv, levels = row_vars),
      wave = factor(wave, levels = waves)
    )
}


# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 7. Build wide results table for one FIRE outcome
# ------------------------------------------------------------

make_wave_results_table <- function(
    dv_name,
    model_waves = fire_dummies_waves,
    row_vars = demo_controls,
    waves = fire_wave_order,
    robust = TRUE
) {

  results_long <- make_wave_results_long(
    dv_name = dv_name,
    model_waves = model_waves,
    row_vars = row_vars,
    waves = waves,
    robust = robust
  ) %>%
    dplyr::mutate(

      result = paste0(
        fmt_num(estimate, 3),
        p_to_stars(p.value),
        " (",
        fmt_num(std.error, 3),
        ")"
      ),

      iv_label = factor(
        iv_label,
        levels = unname(demo_controls_labels[row_vars])
      ),

      wave_label = factor(
        wave_label,
        levels = unname(fire_wave_labels[waves])
      )
    )

  results_wide <- results_long %>%
    dplyr::select(
      iv_label,
      wave_label,
      result
    ) %>%
    tidyr::pivot_wider(
      names_from = wave_label,
      values_from = result
    ) %>%
    dplyr::arrange(iv_label) %>%
    dplyr::rename(
      `Demographic characteristic` = iv_label
    )

  results_wide
}

```

```{r}
make_fire_model <- function(df, dv, iv, controls = character(0)) { #character(0) just means empty character vector so this function works for uncontrolled model then for controlled model
  rhs <- c(iv, controls)
  fml <- as.formula(paste(dv, "~", paste(rhs, collapse = " + ")))
  lm(fml, data = df)
}

fire_dummies_waves <- list()


for (wave_name in names(fire_control_waves)) {#calls list of waves in control waves

  model_list <- list() #fresh model list within each wave

  for (dv in fire_controls) {
    for (iv in demo_controls) { #loop thru dvs, ivs, labels file gives the 4 ivs; fits  models for each outcome

      model_name <- paste0("m_", dv, "_", iv) #ie model using prisonhelp and incarc will be named m_prisonhelp_incarc

      # NOW, actually telling it to run and store the regressions
      model_list[[model_name]] <- make_fire_model(
        df = sample_no_dk,
        dv = dv, 
        iv = iv,
        controls = fire_control_waves[[wave_name]]
      )
    }
  }

  fire_dummies_waves[[wave_name]] <- model_list
}


# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 2. Helpers for extracting and formatting one focal estimate
# ------------------------------------------------------------

p_to_stars <- function(p) {
  dplyr::case_when(
    is.na(p) ~ "",
    p < .001 ~ "***",
    p < .01  ~ "**",
    p < .05  ~ "*",
    TRUE     ~ ""
  )
}

fmt_num <- function(x, digits = 3) {
  ifelse(
    is.na(x),
    "",
    sprintf(paste0("%.", digits, "f"), x)
  )
}


extract_fire_wave_stats <- function(
    dv_name,
    iv_name,
    wave_name,
    model_waves = fire_dummies_waves,
    robust = TRUE
) {

  # Model names follow the naming system created in your main loop:
  # e.g. m_prisonhelp_incarc
  model_name <- paste0("m_", dv_name, "_", iv_name)

  # Check that requested wave exists
  if (!wave_name %in% names(model_waves)) {
    stop("Wave not found: ", wave_name)
  }

  # Pull that wave's model list
  model_list <- model_waves[[wave_name]]

  # Check that requested model exists
  if (!model_name %in% names(model_list)) {
    stop(
      "Model not found in wave '",
      wave_name,
      "': ",
      model_name
    )
  }

  # Pull the actual lm object
  mod <- model_list[[model_name]]

  # Extract coefficient information
  if (robust) {

    ct <- lmtest::coeftest(
      mod,
      vcov. = sandwich::vcovHC(mod, type = "HC1")
    )

    coef_table <- data.frame(
      term = rownames(ct),
      estimate = ct[, 1],
      std.error = ct[, 2],
      p.value = ct[, 4],
      row.names = NULL
    )

  } else {

    sm <- summary(mod)$coefficients

    coef_table <- data.frame(
      term = rownames(sm),
      estimate = sm[, 1],
      std.error = sm[, 2],
      p.value = sm[, 4],
      row.names = NULL
    )
  }

  # The focal coefficient should have the same name as the IV:
  # impact, incarc, knowincarc, or vict
  if (!iv_name %in% coef_table$term) {
    stop(
      "Term '",
      iv_name,
      "' not found in model ",
      model_name
    )
  }

  focal_row <- coef_table[
    coef_table$term == iv_name,
  ]

  # Return one tidy row
  tibble::tibble(
    dv = dv_name,
    dv_label = policy_labels[[dv_name]],
    iv = iv_name,
    iv_label = impact_labels[[iv_name]],
    wave = wave_name,
    wave_label = wave_labels[[wave_name]],
    estimate = focal_row$estimate,
    std.error = focal_row$std.error,
    p.value = focal_row$p.value,
    n = stats::nobs(mod),
    r2 = summary(mod)$r.squared
  )
}
```

```{r}
# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 3. Gather all four IVs x all four waves for one DV
# ------------------------------------------------------------

make_wave_results_long <- function(
    dv_name,
    model_waves = fire_dummies_waves,
    row_vars = demo_controls,
    waves = fire_wave_order,
    robust = TRUE
) {

  # Confirm requested DV belongs to current policy outcome set
  if (!dv_name %in% fire_controls) {
    stop(
      "DV not found in fire_controls: ",
      dv_name
    )
  }

  rows <- lapply(row_vars, function(iv_name) {

    wave_rows <- lapply(waves, function(wave_name) {

      extract_fire_wave_stats(
        dv_label =
          fire_controls_labels[[dv_name]],
        iv_label = demo_controls_labels[[iv_name]],
        wave_name = wave_name,
        model_waves = model_waves,
        robust = robust
      )
    })

    dplyr::bind_rows(wave_rows)
  })

  dplyr::bind_rows(rows) %>%
    dplyr::mutate(
      iv = factor(
        iv,
        levels = row_vars
      ),
      wave = factor(
        wave,
        levels = waves
      )
    )
}


# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 4. Build one wide inspection table for one DV
# ------------------------------------------------------------

make_wave_results_table <- function(
    dv_name,
    model_waves = fire_dummies_waves,
    row_vars = demo_controls,
    waves = fire_wave_order,
    robust = TRUE
) {

  results_long <- make_wave_results_long(
    dv_name = dv_name,
    model_waves = model_waves,
    row_vars = row_vars,
    waves = waves,
    robust = robust
  ) %>%
    dplyr::mutate(

      result = paste0(
        fmt_num(estimate, 3),
        p_to_stars(p.value),
        " (",
        fmt_num(std.error, 3),
        ")"
      ),

      # Preserve demographic row order
      iv_label = factor(
        iv_label,
        levels = unname(demo_controls_labels[row_vars])
      ),

      # Preserve model-wave column order
      wave_label = factor(
        wave_label,
        levels = unname(fire_wave_labels[waves])
      )
    )

  results_wide <- results_long %>%
    dplyr::select(
      iv_label,
      wave_label,
      result
    ) %>%
    tidyr::pivot_wider(
      names_from = wave_label,
      values_from = result
    ) %>%
    dplyr::arrange(iv_label) %>%
    dplyr::rename(
      `Demographic characteristic` = iv_label
    )

  results_wide
}
```
